info.description:
Database-native cognitive architecture for AI agents.

All state lives in the database. The API writes to the same tables the agent reads from.
There is no separate API state — the database is the single source of truth.

## Key Concepts

- **Sessions** — Every agent instance is a session row. RLS isolation, billing, lifecycle.
- **Memory Events** — Immutable append-only ledger. Display state managed via display_modes.
- **Transactions** — Atomic cognition: every thought is a SQL transaction.
- **Tools & Skills** — Progressive disclosure: metadata always visible, full instructions on demand.
- **HITL Approvals** — Human-in-the-loop: pause for review before destructive actions.

## Authentication

Native API endpoints except `/api/v1/health` require a Bearer API key.
`/webhooks/{source}` uses a per-registration HMAC-SHA256 signature instead:
- `cs_ak_*` : admin — full CRUD
- `cs_sk_*` : session — scoped to one session
- `cs_rk_*` : readonly — SELECT only
- `cs_wk_*` : webhook — event ingestion only

Keys are SHA-256 hashed before storage. The full key is only returned at creation time.

Opens a Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream) connection that delivers
real-time session, task, and quarantine events. Clients may pass
?session_id to subscribe to a single session, or omit it to receive
the global stream. Requires a valid Bearer API key: a session-scoped
key (cs_sk_*) may only stream its own session — requests for the
global stream or a foreign session are rejected 403 before any
event-stream header is written.

The global (no session_id) stream is bounded (~5 minutes): it ends
cleanly with a terminal "stream_timeout" event so EventSource
auto-reconnects. Per-session streams are not bounded.

Event payloads vary by type; see the SSEEvent schema for the common
envelope. The first event delivered is always a "connected" event.

Opens the MCP server-initiated message stream (text/event-stream),

post.description:
Accepts a single JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP request and answers the JSON-RPC
response (application/json). Initialize returns the session id in the
Mcp-Session-Id response header; follow-up calls carry it. Every method
except initialize / notifications/initialized / ping requires a session
that completed authenticated initialize — unauthenticated calls answer
HTTP 401 with a JSON-RPC error object (code -32002 Forbidden).
Legacy transports remain available: GET /mcp/sse + POST
/mcp/message?sessionId=...

Mcp-Session-Id.description: Session id for follow-up MCP calls (set by initialize).

202.description: Accepted — the request was a notification (no response body). The answer is intentionally empty (zero bytes), not a JSON document.

400.description: Malformed request (parse error or invalid JSON-RPC envelope).

401.description: Unauthenticated MCP session (unknown/expired Mcp-Session-Id, or a method called before an authenticated initialize). The body is a JSON-RPC error object (code -32002 Forbidden), matching the auth semantics documented in docs/INTEGRATION.md.

405.description: Method not allowed (only GET and POST are served). Answered by chi's default 405 writer with a bare "method not allowed" text body.

501.description: MCP traffic is not served on this mount — bare deployments without the API-level MCP mount answer 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED with the shim stub's NOT_IMPLEMENTED error envelope. Mount consensus serve to reach the real surface.

post.description:
Ingests the raw request body as an external event. The `{source}` value must
match the name, source, or URL path of an enabled row in
`webhook_registrations`. No Bearer API key is required; the server verifies
an HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the exact raw request body using the
registration secret.

Supply the digest in `X-Hub-Signature-256`, `X-Signature-256`, or
`X-Signature` (checked in that order). A leading `sha256=` is optional.
A missing or invalid signature does not reject the request: the event is
stored with `signature_valid=false` and `status=quarantined`, and a new
event still receives `202 Accepted`.

parameters.description: Registered webhook source, name, or URL-path lookup value.
parameters.name: source

parameters.description: Preferred HMAC-SHA256 hex signature; optional `sha256=` prefix.
parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256

parameters.description: Fallback HMAC-SHA256 hex signature; optional `sha256=` prefix.
parameters.name: X-Signature-256

parameters.description: Final fallback HMAC-SHA256 hex signature; optional `sha256=` prefix.
parameters.name: X-Signature

parameters.description: Event type. Falls back to `X-GitHub-Event`, then `unknown`.
parameters.name: X-Event-Type

parameters.description: External delivery identifier used for idempotent ingestion.
parameters.name: X-Delivery-ID

requestBody.description: Raw payload bytes. Sign exactly the bytes sent on the wire.

200.description: Delivery ID was already ingested; returns the existing event ID when available.

202.description: New event accepted, including a new event with an invalid signature.

403.description: The matching webhook registration is disabled.

404.description: No webhook registration matches the source.

413.description: The request body exceeds the 1 MB limit.

429.description: The source exceeded the webhook token-bucket rate limit.

500.description: The request body could not be read or the event could not be stored.
